//: The SECURITY FLOOR for framework pins, as reviewed data the `version-sync` gate judges the RESOLVED lockfile against. WHY THIS IS NOT osv-scan: the osv-scan PR lane is DIFF-AWARE and fails only on NEWLY introduced vulnerabilities, so a tree that has been shipping a vulnerable pin since before the advisory never reds on it — which is exactly the state this harness was in (it shipped `next: 16.2.7` for the two releases after 2026-07-20). The full-tree osv lane is schedule/push-only and network-and-clock dependent, so it cannot be a chain step. This file is the complement: CLOCKLESS, OFFLINE, DETERMINISTIC, and it reds in step 11 on every machine including a developer's with no network. osv-scan owns time-based DISCOVERY; this owns the floor a reviewer has already accepted. NOT A MIRROR OF OSV: one row per advisory a maintainer has read and decided about — a `packages` map that tried to mirror a vulnerability database would be stale the day it shipped and nobody would trust a red from it. `minPatchByMajor` is keyed by MAJOR LINE because that is the shape upstream security releases actually take (one patched release per supported line), and a single flat `minPatch` would wrongly red a consumer legitimately sitting on an older but PATCHED line. A major with NO entry is judged unsupported — derived, not a second hand-maintained `unsupportedMajors` list to drift against this one. OWNERSHIP: harness-OWNED, deliberately NOT seeded and deliberately NOT in ESCAPE_LISTS — `update` refreshes it (a new advisory must reach existing installs, which is the whole point) and `gate-integrity` sha-pins everything under tools/, so a consumer cannot lower a floor without redding step 2. `reviewedUntil` is judged by the scheduled `floor-review` CI job, never by the chain: a wall-clock verdict in `pnpm validate` would red an unchanged tree on a date, which is the exact non-determinism gates-catalog.md rules out.

next.why: apps/web is the API host: it mounts the tRPC router, runs every Server Action, and its proxy.ts sits in front of both. All four HIGH advisories in the July 2026 release land on surfaces this scaffold ships by default, so there is no configuration under which a consumer of this template is out of scope.

advisories.summary: Denial of Service in App Router using Server Actions — crafted requests cause excessive CPU usage that blocks further requests in the same process.
Middleware/proxy bypass in App Router apps built with Turbopack and a single config.i18n.locales entry — any auth or security check the middleware performs is bypassed.
SSRF via rewrites()/redirects() whose external destination hostname is built from request-controlled input; Open Redirect for the redirects case.
SSRF in Server Actions on custom servers — a forwarded or redirected request can be aimed at a malicious host when the attacker controls Host-associated headers.
Unauthenticated disclosure of internal Server Function endpoint ids (reconnaissance).
Denial of Service in the Image Optimization API via malicious remotely-hosted SVGs (self-hosted, default loader, remote images configured).
Unbounded Server Action payload in the Edge runtime leads to memory consumption.
Cache confusion of response bodies for fetch requests whose bodies contain invalid UTF-8 byte sequences.
Cache confusion of response bodies for `fetch(new Request(init), aDifferentInit)` calls carrying request bodies.
